about.title: Mount Shasta Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Mount Shasta draws a steady mix of residents and travelers passing through on I-5, which means grocery stores, gas stations, motels, and outdoor gear shops along N Mt Shasta Boulevard see heavy foot traffic in all kinds of weather. Wet entryways from melting snow, uneven sidewalks near older downtown buildings, and poorly lit parking areas are common settings for falls in this area. California law requires showing that a property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it in time. That's often the hardest part of these claims, and it's why documenting the scene and preserving any surveillance footage matters early. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your claim directly. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened and explain your options under a contingency arrangement, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why This Process Helps in Mount Shasta

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify evidence, like maintenance logs or prior complaints, that speaks to that notice.

items.title: Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Mount Shasta businesses along N Mt Shasta Boulevard and near I-5 use surveillance systems that overwrite footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can matter.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still be able to recover a reduced amount. An attorney can explain how that could apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Mount Shasta?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a claim against a private property owner. If the fall happened on public property, like a city sidewalk or a Caltrans-maintained area near I-5, the deadline is much shorter and involves a separate claims process. An independent attorney can help sort out which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the store or property owner says they didn't know about the hazard?
items.answer: That's actually the central legal question in most premises liability cases. You'd need to show they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the spill, ice, or broken step and failed to address it. This is why photos, witness names, and any available surveillance video from the time of your fall can be so important.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we don't charge you to find an attorney match. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, which means they only get paid if you recover compensation.
